findings.observation: Comprehensive search of supplementary documents, site plan sheets, and reference materials found no Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form submitted to Austin Energy. The Master Comment Report includes an Electric Review section (p. 2-3) indicating Austin Energy has performed a completeness check, but the specific ESPA form referenced in UCM § 1.4.2.6 is not present in the submittal package. Site plan shows preliminary electrical design on Sheet 21, but no documentation that an ESPA form initiated the electric service design process.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires the ESPA form to be submitted to Austin Energy to initiate electric service design and determine transformer/service requirements. For a new 39-unit development, this is a mandatory first step. The absence of this form in the submittal package prevents verification that service requirements have been determined by AE, and allows applicants to self-determine service characteristics. This directly violates the regulatory overview requirement that AE Design holds exclusive determination authority for service characteristics per UCM § 1.3.2.
findings.comment: Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) form has not been submitted to Austin Energy to initiate the electric service design process and determine transformer and service requirements for the 39-unit townhome development. Submit completed ESPA form with point-of-service location, projected electrical load, case number (if applicable), address verification (if applicable), and estimated service date.

findings.observation: No ESPA form located in submittal. Without the form, the point-of-service location cannot be verified. Sheet 21 shows electrical design with transformer locations and routing, but these appear to be preliminary applicant design rather than responsive to AE-determined service location. No documentation exists confirming AE Design has determined and approved the point-of-service location.
findings.reasoning: Point-of-service location is a critical AE Design determination that must be documented in the ESPA submission. The applicant cannot self-determine service location. Its absence from the ESPA (which is missing) prevents verification that AE has made this determination.
findings.comment: Point-of-service location not provided with ESPA form. Include point-of-service location in the completed ESPA submitted to Austin Energy.

findings.observation: No load calculations or electrical demand projections found in supplementary documents or site plan. Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design layout with transformer and service configuration, but no supporting load analysis or demand calculation. No documentation submitted to AE Design specifying the projected electrical load for the 39-unit development.
findings.reasoning: Projected electrical load is a mandatory requirement in the ESPA submission per UCM § 1.4.2.6. This load determines transformer sizing, service capacity requirements, and eligibility for Service-Only vs. infrastructure construction designation. Absence of this calculation prevents AE Design from making proper service determinations.
findings.comment: Projected electrical load not provided with ESPA form. Include electrical demand calculations and load projections in the ESPA submitted to Austin Energy, incorporating anticipated residential electrical demand for 39 units.

findings.observation: No ESPA form located containing estimated service date. Cannot verify whether applicant provided month/year or season estimate for service availability/readiness.
findings.reasoning: The estimated service date is a required field in the ESPA submission per UCM § 1.4.2.6. This timeline helps Austin Energy coordinate construction staging and service activation.
findings.comment: Estimated service date not provided with ESPA form. Include estimated service date (month/year or season) in the ESPA submitted to Austin Energy.

findings.observation: Site plan clearly shows 8 separate buildings (Buildings 1-8) on Sheet 9, containing a total of 39 townhome units. The Building Data Table identifies each building individually (4-plexes, 5-plexes, 6-plexes). However, no separate ESPA form submitted for each building. The absence of multiple ESPA submissions (one per building) prevents verification that AE Design has reviewed individual service requirements for each structure.
findings.reasoning: For multi-building projects, UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires a separate ESPA with building number included for each building to allow AE Design to evaluate individual transformer/service needs. One project-wide ESPA does not satisfy this requirement when multiple buildings with independent service needs exist.
findings.comment: Separate ESPA not submitted for each building in the 8-building project with building number included. Submit individual ESPA forms for each of the 8 buildings (Buildings 1 through 8) with building numbers clearly identified.

findings.observation: Site plan Building Data Table (Sheet 9) shows 39 individual units distributed across 8 buildings. Individual unit addresses/identifiers are noted on Sheet 29 (Addressing Plan). However, no separate ESPA submitted for units. The applicant has submitted a single project-level approach rather than unit-level ESPA submissions for this multi-unit residential project.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, multi-unit projects require separate ESPA submissions for each unit with unit number included. This allows individual service coordination for each residential unit. The absence of unit-level ESPAs prevents verification that AE Design has reviewed individual unit service characteristics.
findings.comment: Separate ESPA not submitted for each unit in the 39-unit multi-unit project with unit number included. Submit individual ESPA forms for each of the 39 units with unit numbers clearly identified.

findings.observation: No Design Intake Form found in supplementary documents. Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes identify a contact person (Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153) and indicate transmission coordination is required, suggesting AE Design involvement is anticipated. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references preliminary design requirements. However, no submitted Design Intake Form for initiating electric design process through AB+C portal is evident.
findings.reasoning: Projects requiring coordination with AE Design for infrastructure work, pole relocation, facility modifications, or buildings increasing load must submit Design Intake Form per UCM § 1.4.2.6. This project has transmission lines requiring clearance coordination and modification constraints, triggering Design Intake Form requirement.
findings.comment: Design Intake Form not submitted to Austin Energy through AB+C portal to initiate electric design process. Submit Design Intake Form for design coordination required for facility modifications, transmission line clearances, and infrastructure interactions.

findings.observation: Master Comment Report confirms Austin Energy has performed a site plan review and completeness check. However, no signed AE Submittal Form located in supplementary documents package. The form that demonstrates AE's agreement to review the site plan and acknowledgment of submittal requirements is missing.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, all sites undergoing land development review requiring Austin Energy coordination must provide a signed AE Submittal Form. This is a standard prerequisite form confirming AE's participation in the review process.
findings.comment: Signed AE Submittal Form not provided. Submit signed AE Submittal Form confirming Austin Energy's participation in land development review.

findings.observation: No AE Standard Notes Form located in supplementary documents. Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy has completed preliminary design review, but the standard form documenting AE's design notes and requirements is not submitted.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, all sites undergoing land development review requiring Austin Energy coordination must provide a signed AE Standard Notes Form establishing which AE standard notes apply to the project.
findings.comment: Signed AE Standard Notes Form not provided. Submit signed AE Standard Notes Form for land development review.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical layout with transformer pads, pull boxes, and service routing, but no supporting electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis documented. No calculations provided verifying that the proposed transformer capacity is adequate for 39 units or substantiating the specific equipment sizing shown.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires load calculations and demand projections be provided to AE Design during land development review. These calculations justify the service specifications and allow AE Design to verify adequacy. Absence of these calculations prevents AE Design review of electrical system adequacy.
findings.comment: Electrical load calculations, demand projections, or capacity analysis not provided to AE Design. Submit electrical load calculations for the 39-unit development, including peak demand projections and justification for transformer sizing and service specifications shown on the site plan.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows preliminary electrical design with transformer and service routing but does not document voltage, phase, capacity specifications in a format submitted to AE Design. No documentation of AE Design approval for the service voltage and size specifications shown on the electrical plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires voltage and service size specifications be provided to AE Design during review. More critically, per regulatory overview, applicants cannot self-certify service specifications - AE Design must determine and approve what voltage, phases, and capacity are available and adequate at the specific location. Showing service specifications without AE Design approval documentation violates UCM § 1.3.2.
findings.comment: Voltage and service size specifications required for service not provided to AE Design with AE approval documentation. Provide AE Design approval letter confirming service voltage, phase configuration, and capacity specifications for the development.

findings.observation: Master Comment Report indicates Austin Energy has provided preliminary design requirements and completed completeness check. However, no formal correspondence or approval letter from AE Design is located in supplementary documents confirming that the preliminary electric design (Sheet 21) has been reviewed and approved by AE Design. The Master Comment Report references a Bluebeam link for AE site comments, but no downloaded AE Design approval letter is evident in the submittal package.
findings.reasoning: Projects requiring AE Design coordination must submit proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electric design per UCM § 1.16.0. The completion of a completeness check does not equate to design approval. Design approval documentation is required to verify that AE Design has reviewed and approved the electric design shown on Sheet 21.
findings.comment: Proof of correspondence with Austin Energy Design approving preliminary electric design not submitted. Provide written AE Design approval letter confirming review and approval of the preliminary electrical design plan.

findings.observation: No service verification letter from Austin Energy stating that utility service can be provided to the site is located in supplementary documents. Unlike water and wastewater utilities, which have explicit 'Suitable and Sufficient Existing Service' approval letters on Sheet 3, no parallel AE service verification letter is present.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, all sites undergoing land development review requiring Austin Energy coordination must submit a letter from Austin Energy confirming that electric service can be provided to the site and identifying any necessary easements or service upgrades. This is a fundamental requirement preceding site plan approval.
findings.comment: Letter from Austin Energy stating utility service can be provided to site and identifying necessary easements or service upgrades not submitted. Request service verification letter from Austin Energy confirming service availability and any required easements.

findings.observation: Consolidated Site Plan Application shows Jason Rodgers (engineer from Bleyl Engineering) signing as the applicant on behalf of the project, with authorization for submittal verification and inspection. However, no separate authorization letter from the property owner (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC) or a designated agent explicitly authorizing representation to Austin Energy is present. The consolidated site plan signature represents authorization for the City of Austin review process but not specifically for Austin Energy coordination.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires either an Agent Authorization Letter specific to Austin Energy review needs or an Owner Authorization Letter explicitly stating 'Austin Energy' when an agent submits on behalf of the owner. A generic application signature does not satisfy this requirement for specific Austin Energy authorization.
findings.comment: Agent Authorization Letter specific to Austin Energy review needs or Owner Authorization Letter explicitly stating 'Austin Energy' not provided. Submit written authorization from property owner (WM 41 Austin RE, LLC) to the agent (Bleyl Engineering) explicitly stating authority to coordinate with Austin Energy and submit electric service documentation.

findings.observation: No documentation of Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee payment or submission located in supplementary documents. No receipt, fee schedule acknowledgment, or payment confirmation found.
findings.reasoning: Per Reviewer Convention, all sites undergoing land development review requiring Austin Energy coordination must pay the Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee. This is a prerequisite for AE's formal review participation.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Site Plan Review fee not provided. Submit payment or documentation of fee payment to Austin Energy for site plan review services.

findings.observation: Sheet 2 displays the historical Mecey Subdivision plat recorded in 1975, which contains only the original dedication of streets and easements with no narrative plat notes. Vision analysis of the sheet confirms the absence of numbered plat notes addressing Austin Energy requirements. No plat notes found covering: (i) Austin Energy pruning/removal rights, (ii) easement and access provision, (iii) owner erosion control and tree protection responsibilities, (iv) clearance maintenance responsibility, or (v-viii) transmission easement restrictions. The project shows transmission easements and multiple utility easements per facts.md, but no accompanying plat notes documenting the requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(8) requires all sites undergoing land development with plat or easement documents to include eight specific plat notes addressing Austin Energy rights, access, owner responsibilities, and transmission easement restrictions. The presence of transmission lines on this site (confirmed by 16-item Electric Transmission Notes on Sheet 3) makes items (v-viii) mandatory. Complete absence of these notes is a critical deficiency.
findings.comment: Plat notes not included as required covering: (i) Austin Energy pruning/removal rights, (ii) easement and access provision, (iii) owner erosion control and tree protection responsibilities, (iv) clearance maintenance responsibility, and (v-viii) transmission easement restrictions. Add all eight required plat notes to the site plan or create a new plat amendment with these notes.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 Electric Transmission Notes (item 16 and throughout the section) establish that transmission easements exist on the property with strict restrictions prohibiting habitable structures, storage sheds, drainage/detention ponds, and other structures that would impair AE access. Sheet 31 shows a landscape plan. Facts.md identifies transmission easement existence on the property but does not specify exact boundaries. Vision analysis of Sheet 3 confirmed the transmission easement requirements are documented but cannot visually confirm the exact spatial footprint of the transmission easement relative to proposed parkland designations on the landscape plan without additional detailed examination. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) cannot be fully evaluated for parkland designation conflicts with transmission easement location without comparative spatial analysis.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(9) prohibits land within transmission easements from being labeled as parkland or proposed for parkland dedication. This is a critical restriction violation if transmission easements overlap with landscape/parkland areas. The facts and Electric Transmission Notes confirm transmission easements exist; however, without access to the specific transmission easement boundary overlay and detailed landscape plan parkland designation boundaries, a definitive determination cannot be made. The requirement necessitates visual confirmation of coordinate/spatial relationships.
findings.comment: Cannot definitively verify from available evidence whether land within transmission easement is correctly excluded from parkland designation or reserved for parkland dedication. Provide explicit identification of transmission easement boundaries on landscape and plat plans with clear notation that no parkland or permanent structures are located within easement areas.

findings.observation: Master Comment Report indicates Electric Review is complete and preliminary design requirements were provided. Sheet 21 shows electrical design layout but no survey demonstrating proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities. No proximity survey document located in supplementary documents. Facts.md indicates transmission easements exist, and Sheet 3 transmission notes document 20-25 foot clearance requirements from transmission structures, but no formal survey proving compliance with these clearances is submitted.
findings.reasoning: When AE Design requires proximity surveys to document customer facilities maintain required clearances from AE primary voltage facilities, this survey must be submitted per UCM § 1.10.3. Given the presence of transmission lines and the multiple clearance requirements documented on Sheet 3, AE Design may have required such a survey. The absence of this survey prevents verification of clearance compliance.
findings.comment: Survey not provided showing proximities of customer's existing and/or proposed facilities to existing AE primary voltage facilities as may be required by AE Design. If requested by AE, submit professional survey documenting clearances between proposed buildings, utilities, and equipment from all AE primary voltage transmission facilities.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) displays electrical service infrastructure with transformer pads, pull boxes, and service routing. However, no documentation is evident that the service characteristics shown (voltage, phases, capacity) have been determined and approved by AE Design. The plan appears to be applicant-prepared preliminary design rather than responsive to AE Design determinations. No AE Design approval letter confirming the service specifications are available and appropriate for the location is submitted.
findings.reasoning: Per UCM § 1.3.2, AE Design holds exclusive determination authority for service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) available at any location. Applicants cannot self-certify service specifications. Plans showing service specifications without documentation of AE Design determination and approval directly violate this code section. The regulatory overview emphasizes this as a common violation pattern (violation #1).
findings.comment: Plans show service characteristics (voltage, phases, capacity) without documentation of AE Design determination and approval. Provide AE Design approval letter confirming the service voltage, phases, and capacity shown on Sheet 21 have been determined as available and approved for the site's location and load requirements.
